description:
FILED s461ar as the measured residue of #911, which closed the two runtime
write sites (`$1 =~ s///` and `$1 =~ tr///` now die perl's death).  These four
shapes never REACH those sites: PCL boxes the value first, so the write lands
in a throwaway box and the program carries on.  Probed 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl,
each inside `eval { ... }`:

    $+ =~ s/b/B/                         perl DIES   PCL no error
    for my $v ("lll") { $v =~ s/l/L/ }   perl DIES   PCL no error
    sort { $a =~ s/./X/; 0 } (...)       perl DIES   PCL no error
    $_ =~ s/m/M/ for ("mmm");            perl DIES   PCL no error

perl's message is the same "Modification of a read-only value attempted" in all
four.  ($1, $& and the rest of the capture family DO reach the sites and now
agree -- Pl/t/caret-vars-01.t's #911 row is the 12-case table.)

WHAT THE FIX IS: not another write site.  It is a READ-ONLY MARK on the box:
perl marks the SV read-only and every mutator asks.  A foreach over a literal
list, sort's $a/$b, and $+ would each be created with the mark set, and
box-set / the two regex sites / the compound assigns would ask it.  That is the
same mark #873 needed for captures and %p-array-readonly-p already has for
array STORAGE, so the three should end up as one mechanism rather than three.

Do NOT implement it as another special case at the s///+tr/// sites: those two
already do the right thing, and the shapes above are wrong at the moment the
box is CREATED.

BAR: the four rows above vs perl; the #911 12-row table unmoved; full sweep
(a read-only mark on foreach-literal boxes is on a very hot path -- measure the
counting-loop bench rows).

=== DESIGN FINDING, s462at (agent AT, round 19).  NOT shipped; measured and
=== sized instead.  Two of the task's own premises turned out to be FALSE, and
=== that is the finding: there is no mark to reuse, and the family is wider
=== than s///.

(1) THE PREMISE "shared with #873's read-only-capture mechanism" DOES NOT HOLD.
#873 did NOT ship a mark.  Read its own SHIPPED section: it is ONE COMPILER
PREDICATE (`Pl::ExprToCL::_capture_read_group`) plus TWO WRITE SLOTS (the `=`
lowering and `open`'s handle argument) plus two runtime helpers.  Option (i),
"make a capture a read-only BOX", was explicitly sized and REJECTED there for
its hot-path cost.  So there is nothing to reuse: #873 marks nothing.
The other candidate, `%p-array-readonly-p`, is REPRESENTATIONAL and
array-only â a read-only array IS a simple vector (no fill pointer), which is
why reading costs nothing.  A scalar has no such spare representation, and
`p-box` has no spare flag: its seven slots are value/nv/nv-ok/sv/sv-ok/class/
is-ref, and adding an eighth grows EVERY box in the image.

(2) $+ IS ALREADY RIGHT â the task's first row is stale.  #911 shipped in the
same session that filed this, and `$+ =~ s/b/B/` now dies in PCL as in perl
(probed on 4c354bc AND on the s462at tree: both ERR).  The only residue there
is a VALUE: perl leaves `$+` as "b" because it refuses before running,
PCL clears the capture group while matching and then dies, so `$+` reads "".
Three shapes remain, not four.

(3) THE FAMILY IS WIDER THAN s///, and that settles the fix's LAYER.  Probed
5.40.3 vs ./runpcl, identical on 4c354bc and on the s462at tree:

    for my $v ("lll") { $v =~ s/l/L/ }   perl DIES   PCL ok
    for my $v ("lll") { $v = "X" }       perl DIES   PCL ok    <- NEW
    for my $v ("lll") { chop $v }        perl DIES   PCL ok    <- NEW
    for my $v (1,2)   { $v++ }           perl DIES   PCL ok    <- NEW
    sort { $a =~ s/./X/; 0 } (â¦)         perl DIES   PCL ok
    $_ =~ s/m/M/ for ("mmm");            perl DIES   PCL ok
  controls, all SAME:
    for my $v (@a) { $v =~ s/l/L/ }      an ordinary alias WRITES, both
    for my $v (1..2) { $v++ }            a RANGE's elements are modifiable in
                                         perl too â the literal rule does NOT
                                         extend to range-produced values
    sort { $a cmp $b } â¦                 reading $a/$b
    "abc"=~/(b)/; print $+               reading $+

So it is not "three more write sites"; it is EVERY mutator, which is exactly
the task's own conclusion and is why the mark has to be set where the box is
CREATED.  It also means a per-write-site fix is not merely inelegant, it is
unbounded.

(4) THE MECHANISM THAT DOES EXIST, and its price.  A magic cell with a DYING
setter is available today and costs other boxes nothing:
    (make-p-box (make-p-magic-cell :getter (lambda () VAL)
                                   :setter (lambda (v) (%p-readonly-modification))))
`box-set` already delegates to a cell's setter and `unbox`/`to-string`/
`to-number` already read through its getter, so every mutator in the runtime
asks without a single new test.  THE PRICE is on the READ side and it is not
free: every read of the loop variable becomes an out-of-line getter funcall,
and `for my $v (LIST) { â¦ }` over literals is a shape the counting-loop bench
rows contain.  That has to be measured before it is chosen â the same
measurement %p-no-overload-possible-p's comment records for its own ordering.

(5) THE THREE SITES ARE THREE DIFFERENT EMISSIONS, which is the real cost:
    * a foreach LIST's literal elements â Pl/Parser.pm's `_foreach_alias_rewrite`
      / Parser2's `_alias_box_form` decide the element forms today, and the
      s369 `(vector E1 â¦ Ek)` rule is what would carry the read-only boxes;
    * the statement-MODIFIER `EXPR for (LIST)` â a second lowering of the same
      list;
    * sort's `$a`/`$b` â bound by the sort lowering, not by a list at all.
  All three are in the foreach/sort emission region, which is where the
  boxed-aggregates and foreach-range performance work lives.  A round that
  ships this should own that region for the session.

RECOMMENDATION: the magic-cell-with-a-dying-setter, gated on a MEASURED
counting-loop bench A/B, in a session that also owns the foreach lowering.
Do NOT add a slot to p-box, and do NOT add per-mutator checks: (3) shows the
mutator set is the whole language.  If the bench says the getter funcall costs
too much, the fallback is to accept the divergence and register it in
docs/not-supported.md â perl's read-only literals are a diagnostic, not a
value the program consumes, so rule 12's boundary (fable-answers-s329 Â§1)
puts it on the ANNOUNCE side rather than the DIE side.

BAR (unchanged from the task, plus): the twelve rows in (3) vs perl; the #911
12-row table in Pl/t/caret-vars-01.t unmoved; the counting-loop bench rows
measured BEFORE and after; full sweep.


s463f (Fable, 2026-09-01) PROBE ADDED to the family â #939 changed one shape from an ACCIDENTAL death to the silent write this task covers: `for my $e ("const") { substr($e,0,1) =~ s/c/C/ }` DIED on 12eacb5 (the substr target was an rvalue string, so #911 killed it for the wrong reason: no place, not read-only) and is a silent write on 6e6f191 (the target is now the foreach-alias box, which carries no read-only mark).  perl dies read-only in all three spellings (`$e =~ s///`, `substr($e,..) =~ s///`, `substr($e,..) = ...`); PCL now agrees with ITSELF (no death in any) â the consistent state this task sizes.  No baseline row depended on the accidental death (AT sweep TOTAL +0, gate green).  Probe file: scratchpad probes/p936.pl of session 16e00e26.

s463f (Fable, AU review) ONE MORE SPELLING for the family: the 4-argument `substr("lit", 0, 1, "X")` on a LITERAL dies read-only in perl (inside eval: trapped) and is SILENT in PCL on 6e6f191 and after #960(b) alike.  AU's #960 note explains why the runtime cannot die there: `substr(f(), 0, 2, "AB")` on a TEMPORARY is legal perl (the write is discarded, the call answers "he"), and a raw CL string cannot be told from a literal -- which is exactly the read-only MARK this task is about.  Probe scratchpad probes/au960c.pl.
subject: read-only residue after #911: $+, a foreach over a LITERAL and sort's $a accept s/// where perl dies
